title: InvenSense MPU-6050 IMU
note: A 6-axis MEMS IMU (3-axis gyroscope + 3-axis accelerometer), built to show how one works from the outside in: the QFN package, the CMOS chip on its lead frame, the MEMS chip bonded face down on it, and the six sensors in the MEMS layer. Frame: z up, package bottom at z = 0, centred in x and y; +X and +Y as the datasheet's orientation figure (pin 1 top left in the top view, pins 1-6 down the -X side, 7-12 along -Y, 13-18 up +X, 19-24 along +Y). Real size in metres (the package is 4 mm). Layer thicknesses and the MEMS fine structure are estimates: no free cross-section of any consumer IMU exists (open_questions).

reference_model.note: No 3D model of the MPU-6050's inside exists; layout from the die photos (zeptobars_mpu6050), package from the datasheet drawing (mpu6050_ds 11.2).

cmos_die_x.quote: Size of big die is 2782x2718 µm, small die - 2778x2195 µm.

cmos_die_y.quote: Size of big die is 2782x2718 µm

pin_1_mark.value: laser-marked dot on top, at pin 1 (top left corner in the top view); about 0.55 mm across, centred 0.40 mm from the left edge and 0.52 mm from the top edge (part of the marking decal)
pin_1_mark.quote: PIN 1 IDENTIFIER IS A LASER MARKED FEATURE ON TOP

also.quote: size and position measured on the photo rectified by the package's four corners to the 4.00 mm body (200 px/mm): dot 99-120 px across, centre (81, 105) px

marking.value: laser marking on top: pin 1 dot, then INVENSENSE / MPU-6050 / lot code / foundry, vendor, year-week and rev codes, over the whole 4 x 4 mm top
marking.quote: INVENSENSE MPU6050 XXXXXX-XX XX YYWW X ... Part number ... Lot traceability code ... Foundry code ... Package Vendor Code ... Rev Code

also.quote: traced: photo rectified by the package's four corners at (254, 300), (1003, 300), (1004, 1049), (257, 1053) px to 800 x 800 px; median 9 px, minus a 30 px blurred background, threshold 9, specks under 150 px dropped, 7 px closing. The V of INVENSENSE and the left stroke of the M are worn in the photo and were drawn in at the other letters' 13 px stroke width. This chip reads D2G594-L1 / EI 1228 D

exposed_pad_chamfer.quote: C0.3 (bottom view, at the exposed pad's corner nearest pin 1)

bonded_pins.quote: NC ... Not internally connected. May be used for PCB trace routing. (pins 2, 3, 4, 5, 14, 15, 16, 17)
bonded_pins.note: only connected pins get a wire bond; RESV pins (19, 21, 22) are counted as bonded (estimated: 'Do not connect' means used internally)

stack.value: lead frame with exposed pad; CMOS chip glued on the pad; MEMS chip face down on the CMOS chip, joined by Al-Ge eutectic bonds that also seal the cavity; the MEMS handle wafer is the lid; gold wires from the CMOS bond pads to the leads; all in mould compound
stack.quote: Eutectic bonding between a germanium layer deposited on the MEMS and the top aluminum layer on the CMOS simultaneously creates multiple interconnects and a hermetic seal ... After bonding, a portion of the MEMS wafer is removed by conventional dicing saw cuts to expose the CMOS wire bond pads ... Each die is fully encapsulated and is packaged using standard, low-cost QFN packages
stack.also: zeptobars_mpu6050: "It contains 2 dies, soldered/welded face-to-face in multiple places"

electrodes_under_mems.value: aluminium electrodes on the CMOS chip's top layer under the moving plates; logic under the MEMS outside the cavities
electrodes_under_mems.quote: The top layer of CMOS aluminum provides electrodes for actuation and sensing ... The process also allows circuits under the MEMS outside the small cavity areas

mems_device_layer.source: nasiri2010, p.62 (range); 40 µm chosen inside it (estimated)
mems_device_layer.quote: Using a bulk silicon device layer allows for thicker MEMS structures (20-100µm)

thicknesses.source: nasiri2010 (stack order only); thicknesses estimated: no source gives them, chosen so the stack (lead frame 0.20 + attach + CMOS + gap + device + handle = 0.71 mm) sits under the 0.90 mm package top with room for the wire loops

die_placement.value: CMOS die centred on the exposed pad, its 2782 µm side along X; MEMS die centred on the CMOS die, leaving bond-pad strips about 260 µm wide along both Y edges of the CMOS die
die_placement.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, estimated from mpu6050-big-HD.jpg (2.35 px/µm): pad strips along the top and bottom edges, seal-ring footprint between; the die's rotation in the package is not known (open question)

value.frame: measured on mpu6050-small-top-HD.jpg, x right, y down from the die's top left corner, in µm; the die lies face down, so in the model x is mirrored

mems_layout_um.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, estimated from mpu6050-small-top-HD.jpg, scaled by the 2778 µm die width (2.35 px/µm); accelerometer cells, springs and paddles from full-resolution crops of its bottom row
mems_layout_um.used_for: the electrodes under the gyro plates and the sensor axes; the sensors themselves are traced (facts.die_trace)

axes.gyros: left = Z, middle = Y, right = X: nasiri2010 Fig. 7, an InvenSense die photo captioned "MPU-3000, 3-Axis gyroscope in 2.8mm x 2.4mm" and labelled "Z-Axis", "Y-Axis", "X-Axis" left to right; the MPU-6050 die's top row has the same three structures in the same order and orientation (compared by eye: left two stacked plates with comb banks above and below, middle one large plate, right two masses with vertical comb arrays)
axes.accelerometers: derived, not labelled in any source: the die's X and Y directions follow from the sourced gyros: nasiri2010 p.62-63 says the X gyro's two masses move out of plane in opposition and the Coriolis forces turn its sense frame in plane, which for rotation about X needs the masses apart along X; the X gyro's two masses sit side by side across the die and the Y gyro's are stacked, so across the die is X and along it is Y (the same in both photos, mirror or not). Left accelerometer: hung on long beams running along Y and with comb fingers along Y, so it moves along X: X axis. Middle: the same design turned 90 degrees: Y axis. Right: two masses on a centre beam over electrodes, a teeter-totter: Z axis
axes.quote: coupled dual-mass (tuning fork) proof-masses that are driven out-of-plane and generate Coriolis forces in-plane ... The Coriolis torque moves the four-bar linkage which is sensed in-plane using capacitive electrodes

die_trace.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, traced from mpu6050-small-top-HD.jpg (6704 x 5312, CC BY 3.0) at 2.35 px/µm with the die's top left corner at (80, 80) px
die_trace.method: each region (µm on the photo, x right, y down) cut into 2 µm cells; a cell is a gap when 40% or more of its pixels are darker than 105 (of 255), else silicon; specks and pinholes under 12 cells removed, no smoothing (it erased the 4-5 µm comb fingers). Masks and the photo crops (1.0 px/µm) in refs/mpu6050/die/. The photo is the device layer's face towards the CMOS chip; in the model it lies face down, so it is mirrored across X and the photo is shown on the layer's top
die_trace.split: each sensor is two parts: <sensor>_masses, the silicon the photo shows dim, and <sensor>_frame, the bright rest. The mean of a cell's silicon pixels (those 105 and brighter) under 160 makes it dim; dim or bright islands under 40 cells join their surroundings. Brightness profiles across the Z gyro show anchored bars and combs at 175-195 and the plates and the comb fingers between the fixed ones at 120-140, so dim is read as moving; it is a cue from the photo, not a drawing, and some fine moving parts come out bright
die_trace.limits: trenches under about 1 µm (between comb teeth) are not cut, only seen in the photo; debris on the die reads as gaps in places (accelerometers, lower right)

wire_bonds.source: mil_std_883_2010, 3.2.1.1 and 3.2.1.3 (limits); values, in wire diameters, chosen inside them (ball height and crescent thickness are not in the standard: estimated)
wire_bonds.quote: Gold ball bonds on the die or package post wherein the ball bond diameter is less than 2.0 times or greater than 5.0 times the wire diameter ... Tailless bonds on the die or package post that are less than 1.2 times or more than 5.0 times the wire diameter in width, or are less than 0.5 times or more than 3.0 times the wire diameter in length

bond_wires.source: nasiri2010 (wires from CMOS pads exposed beside the MEMS die); diameter, loop height and pad size estimated (no source gives them); pad strip width estimated from zeptobars_mpu6050 mpu6050-big-HD.jpg
bond_wires.quote: a portion of the MEMS wafer is removed by conventional dicing saw cuts to expose the CMOS wire bond pads
bond_wires.note: pins 6-13 bond to the pads along the -Y edge, pins 18-24 and 1 to the +Y edge, each strip in the order of its leads (estimated)

cmos_photo.value: the CMOS die's face shown with ZeptoBars' photo of it: mpu6050-big-HD.jpg cropped to the die's edges at (80, 95) and (6625, 6512) px (2.353 x 2.361 px/µm over the 2782 x 2718 µm die, as the MEMS photo's 2.35), at 0.5 px/µm. Only the band under the MEMS die is used (the die centred, rows 712-5895 px, refs/mpu6050/die/cmos.jpg): outside it the pad strips are covered with residue from separating the dies, which an intact chip doesn't have, so the strips show the die's clean surface (materials.cmos_surface) and aluminium pads (materials.cmos_aluminium). Its pattern is the MEMS layout mirrored (the Z accelerometer bottom left, the Z gyro top right), as a face-down MEMS die needs, so the photo is used unmirrored with its top at +Y. Residue from separating the dies covers most of the bond-pad strips (pads show only near the corners, about 85 µm square), so the pads stay estimated
cmos_photo.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, File:Mpu6050-big-HD.jpg (6699 x 6611, CC BY 3.0): "Larger die of the Invensense MPU6050 integrated gyroscope and accelerometer"

electrodes.source: nasiri2010, p.62-63 (electrodes under the torsion plates); their layout shows in the CMOS photo (facts.cmos_photo); the 1 µm top-metal thickness (used for the photo face and the bond pads) is estimated
electrodes.quote: Aluminum electrodes on the IC are located under the torsion plates forming parallel-plate electrodes

gyro_structures.value: X/Y gyros: dual proof masses driven out of plane (tuning fork) on torsion plates over CMOS electrodes; Z gyro: two masses resonated in plane, flexibly coupled; comb electrodes for in-plane drive and sense
gyro_structures.quote: coupled dual-mass (tuning fork) proof-masses that are driven out-of-plane ... torsion plates ... Aluminum electrodes on the IC are located under the torsion plates forming parallel-plate electrodes ... two proof-masses that are resonated in-plane ... flexibly coupled

gyro_frequencies_khz.quote: X-Axis 30 33 36 kHz; Y-Axis 27 30 33 kHz; Z-Axis 24 27 30 kHz

accelerometer.value: one proof mass per axis, sensed differentially by capacitance
accelerometer.quote: uses separate proof masses for each axis. Acceleration along a particular axis induces displacement on the corresponding proof mass, and capacitive sensors detect the displacement differentially

comb_teeth.quote: Width of the smallest teethes is 1µm
comb_teeth.note: the teeth (about 5.3 µm pitch, measured on the photo) are finer than the 2 µm trace, so they show in the photo on the traced fingers, not as geometry

cmos_aluminium.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, mpu6050-HD.jpg: CMOS die's top metal, 3 spots averaged at (438, 284), (460, 361), (416, 416) px (microscope lighting)

cmos_surface.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, mpu6050-big-HD.jpg: the CMOS die's face over its logic, 3 spots averaged at (1500, 4680), (1800, 5100), (900, 4980) px (microscope lighting)

silicon.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, mpu6050-HD.jpg: MEMS die's top frame, 3 spots averaged at (1707, 350), (1641, 459), (1575, 613) px (microscope lighting)

mems_structure.source: zeptobars_mpu6050, mpu6050-HD.jpg: MEMS structures, 2 spots averaged at (1455, 317), (1422, 438) px (microscope lighting)

mould_compound.source: spekking_nexus7: package top away from the marking (more than 10 px from any marking, 30 px in from the edges), mean of 313,000 px on the rectified photo; roughness by eye (matte, speckled)

laser_marking.source: spekking_nexus7: inside the traced marking (eroded 3 px), mean of 62,500 px on the rectified photo

open_questions: Layer thicknesses (CMOS die, handle wafer, bond gap, cavity) are estimates: no free cross-section of the MPU-6050 or any consumer IMU was found.
Device layer: 40 µm chosen inside the paper's 20-100 µm range; Zeptobars' "MEMS part is 28µm above surface ... on smaller die - 100 µm above" is not explained enough to use.
Accelerometer axes are derived (die axes from the sourced gyros, each mass's direction from its springs and combs), not labelled by any source.
The dies' rotation inside the package and which edges carry the bond pads relative to the pins: estimated.

Lead-frame NiPdAu finish and gold wire colour need a sourced photo (the board photo shows the leads soldered); the shared foil_silver and foil_gold stand in. Mould and marking colours are from one photo, under its lighting.
Corner tie-bar ends of the lead frame (the datasheet's corner detail, dimension a) are left out: a is not in the table.

The device layer is traced from one photo of a delayered die: comb teeth (1 µm) are only in the photo, debris reads as gaps in places, and moving and anchored parts are one piece per sensor (the photo shows anchored parts brighter, moving ones dimmer).

budget.note: the inside carries the traced device layer (about 91k triangles, 5.9 MB) and its die photos (1.1 MB, plus 0.5 MB for the CMOS face); it loads only when Internal is pressed
